Highlight Clip: a16z Crypto Partner: Finance Remains Blockchain's Clearest Near-Term Application Opportunity a16z Crypto Partner: Finance Remains Blockchain's Clearest Near-Term Application Opportunity a16z Crypto General Partner Guy Wuollet said in an October 6 interview on the official a16z crypto channel that blockchain's clearest near-term opportunities remain in finance, particularly stablecoins and perpetuals. a16z is also focused on payments, lending, credit, exchanges, prediction markets, derivatives, crypto-AI, and wealth management. Wuollet said stablecoin demand is driven by payment efficiency and demand for U.S. dollars in high-inflation or capital-controlled markets. He sees stablecoins and blockchains as driving finance's digital transformation, much as cloud services transformed enterprise IT. — link

Highlight Clip: Star Xu: Bitcoin Nearly Died Several Times, but Crypto Emerged Stronger Star Xu: Bitcoin Nearly Died Several Times, but Crypto Emerged Stronger In an interview on the New Era Finance Podcast, OKX founder and CEO Star Xu recalled Bitcoin's early forks and hash power attacks, the collapse of Mt. Gox, disagreements over scaling, and the later FTX incident. He said Bitcoin had nearly "died" several times and that resolving industry crises could take months or even a year. In his view, once those problems are resolved, the industry becomes better, bigger, and stronger than before. — link

Spot Bitcoin ETFs Recorded $82.39 Million in Net Outflows, While Spot Ethereum ETFs Saw $69.68 Million in Net Outflows on October 16 (ET) On October 16 (ET), spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded total net outflows of $82.39 million, led by BlackRock's IBIT with $71.78 million in net outflows. Spot Ethereum ETFs recorded total net outflows of $69.68 million, marking their third consecutive day of net outflows, with all of the day's net outflows coming from BlackRock's ETHA. — link

Bitget's English Terms of Use, Marked as Updated Oct. 16, List Russia, Belarus and Kazakhstan Among Prohibited Jurisdictions According to The Defiant, Bitget will discontinue services for certain users, with account-specific deadlines and withdrawal instructions sent directly to those affected. The exchange described it as a one-off exercise, said user funds remain safe, and noted that users who receive no notification can continue using their accounts under its terms. Its official support account also cited the prohibited-jurisdiction list when responding to restrictions on Russian users. One affected user reported an Oct. 21 deadline, but Bitget's main announcement gave no common deadline, affected account count or specific regulatory basis. — link
